title: retry workflow log grouping: title each PR group with its full GitHub PR URL, not its number
answers: Retry job logs group by PR number, which makes reruns hard to find
Where is the per-PR log group header built in the retry workflow?
How are PR numbers and SHAs passed from the retry job into retry.sh?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/retry.yml (the retry job step) reads `number sha` pairs for each PR, opens a `::group::` per PR, and calls `bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/retry.sh"` with the args and `$GH_REPO`, `$sha`.
Rule: Build the group title from the repo and number, `::group::https://github.com/$GH_REPO/pull/$number`, so each collapsed log section is a clickable, self-identifying PR link. Keep the group wrapper around the retry.sh call; the arguments passed to retry.sh are unchanged.
Symptom: Collapsed log groups read only "PR #<number>" with no repository, so a reader scanning a retry run could not tell which repo's PR a section referred to or easily jump to it.
Constraints: Only the log group title changes. Does not affect retry.sh output, annotations, or which PRs are processed. Skipped rows (empty number) still `continue` before the group is opened.
applies: Scope: the per-PR group title in the retry workflow's log output in .github/workflows/retry.yml.
says: Collapsed retry log sections only show pull request numbers without identifying the repository.
We cannot easily jump to the relevant pull request from the collapsed retry logs.
Show full clickable pull request links in the headers of retry job log sections.
Make each collapsed log group in the retry workflow display the direct pull request address.
search: In .github/workflows/retry.yml, per-PR log groups are titled using the full pull request URL format ::group::https://github.com/$GH_REPO/pull/$number rather than just the pull request number. This makes each collapsed log section a clickable link identifying the repository and pull request during retry job execution. The change is strictly scoped to the log group header in retry.yml, leaving retry.sh arguments, annotations, and PR processing behavior unchanged.
